For a complete mode workflow, use a PDK notebook from [Choose a simulation](../start/choose-a-simulation.qmd#getting-started).
This backend reference uses the shared `snapshot` from
[source observations](inspect-the-source.qmd) and the Palace preparation
extra. Eigenmode asks for resonances of the configured field model. It does not
require a surface-loss model, junction port or EPR request merely to run.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import display
from scgsim.meshing import FeatureRecipe
from scgsim.palace import EigenmodeSim

sim = EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_plan(snapshot)
sim.set_output_dir(Path(".artifacts/public-xmon-palace-modes"))
sim.set_eigenmode(num_modes=2, target=2e9, tolerance=1e-6, save=0)
sim.set_mesh(recipe=FeatureRecipe(), quality_threshold=0.01)
sim.set_numerical(amr_max_passes=0)
display(sim.input_summary())
```

`set_mesh(...)` chooses how the mesh is sized and checked: `recipe` sets the
initial element sizes, `mesher` the Gmsh algorithms and the geometry order,
`budgets` how hard the repair loop tries, and `quality_threshold` the minimum
signed inverse condition number (minSICN) every tetrahedron must reach. This example passes the defaults,
`FeatureRecipe()` and `0.01`, so you can see where to change them; leaving
`set_mesh` out gives the same mesh. Geometric order describes the mesh
representation and is independent of Palace's FEM order. The recipes, their
parameters and what happens when a mesh cannot reach the threshold are in the
shared [Palace mesh controls](../reference/specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls).

These are explicit example controls: target is in hertz and recipe sizes are in
micrometres. Choose them in relation to the mode and quantities your
SCQ study needs, and retain the chosen settings and any later changes in the
study notes. `save` controls native saved-field output. A fresh
`EigenmodeSim` writes `Nonconformal=true`. This single-mesh example explicitly
sets `amr_max_passes=0`, which disables adaptive refinement. Before
`write_config()`, provide `amr_max_passes` through `set_numerical(...)`; a
positive pass limit also requires caller-selected `amr_tolerance` and
`amr_update_fraction`, or, with a convergence declaration (below), only
`amr_update_fraction`. Later calls that omit these controls retain their
current values. Record selected numerical and output controls beside the
action they govern rather than hiding them in notebook helpers.

Read the summary's configured mode/search/resource choices against your study.
It displays normalized source and settings without meshing or solving. The
vacuum envelope came from the plan, and the unspecified external Eigenmode
surface retains Palace's natural PMC condition; HFSS assigns the same condition,
Perfect H, on the faces of its Region.

## Declare when refinement has converged

With adaptive refinement, say which numbers must settle instead of giving
Palace a tolerance. The thresholds below show the form; choose your own:

```python
from scgsim.palace import ErrorIndicator, ModeFrequency, SurfaceEpr

sim.set_numerical(amr_max_passes=8, amr_update_fraction=0.7)
sim.set_convergence(
    ModeFrequency(modes=[1]).within(percent=0.001),
    SurfaceEpr.each("MA", "MS", "SA", margin_um=1.0).within(percent=2),
    ErrorIndicator().below(1e-2),
)
```

`amr_max_passes=8` allows eight refinements, so nine solves; each solve is one
pass, and pass 1 solves the mesh `mesh()` writes. Mode 1's frequency holds at a
pass when it moved by at most 0.001 % since the pass before. The
Surface-EPR line declares one criterion per interface kind, each on that kind's
participation beyond 1 µm of every mode; it needs the plan's
`set_surface_epr` with all three specs, each asking for that
[margin](#surface-epr-margin-rows), before `prepare()`. The whole-surface participation is left out on purpose: it kept
growing with every refinement on the layouts measured, so a change criterion
on it would not hold. With a declaration Palace's own tolerance no longer
ends the run, so `amr_tolerance` is left out: `write_config()` refuses it and
names the `ErrorIndicator().below(...)` line to write instead. It also refuses
`ModeFrequency(modes=[3])` while `num_modes=2`, and a kind that
`set_epr_request(surface_interfaces=...)` leaves out.

Palace stops at the first pass where every criterion has held, so the solves
after it are not run (the stop comes one to two seconds after that pass); a run
that does not converge runs all nine. The
returned run's `result.convergence` and the trust report say at which pass every
criterion had held, which one held last and after which pass SCGSim stopped
Palace, or which one still fails at the last pass and by how much against its
threshold. The
[Eigenmode contract](../reference/specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#eigenmode-convergence) and
the shared [convergence declaration](../reference/specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-declaration)
list every quantity and check.

## Build the real backend inputs

```python
mesh_path = sim.mesh()
config_path = sim.write_config()
print(mesh_path, config_path)
```

After meshing, `sim.mesh_summary()` exposes detached generation observations.
For Eigenmode it also reports a topological Nédélec degree-of-freedom estimate
for the configured FEM order. This estimate is not the solver's actual DOF
count; changing FEM order refreshes it without regenerating the mesh.

Meshing builds the source geometry with SGB into a conformal model, then meshes it
with `scgsim.meshing` until every tetrahedron reaches the quality threshold, or stops with
`MeshRepairError` ([what that means](../reference/specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls)).
The finite-metal PEC shell excludes conductor interiors from
Palace solution domains. Config writing uses the resulting exact mesh/index
identity. Changing source geometry or mesh controls invalidates derived state;
prepare a new snapshot when the shared source changes rather than overriding
only its stack or envelope.

At this point you have no eigenfrequency result. Continue to
[solver observations](inspect-the-prepared-model.qmd) and
[explicit execution](run-elsewhere.qmd), then
[returned result resolution](convergence-and-reports.qmd). Read the requested mode
frequency and any selected participation history for the
[intended SCQ use](convergence-and-reports.qmd#interpret-for-scq-use), with native
criteria/status retained. An eigenpair residual or AMR indicator describes its
own native quantity; it does not by itself establish adequacy of the frequency
or EPR contribution you plan to use.

On return, the report retains a native `eig.csv` `Q=+inf` as
**native-reported infinite Q**. Its finite Q-based view is unavailable. Keep
that native observation separate from a physical lossless-model claim; it
does not replace a missing loss assumption or determine a device lifetime.
Other otherwise valid frequency and energy channels remain readable under
their existing contracts. The [native Q contract](../reference/specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#native-eigenmode-q)
defines this narrow allowance; other columns and NaN/negative infinity remain
subject to their current policies.

For the public Xmon with an inductive source port and attributed thin films,
use the [Palace EPR extension](xmon/palace.qmd) **before** meshing
and handoff preparation. Its surface/bulk/port selections filter reported
quantities; they do not delete physical domains or change normalization.
The [EPR concept](../concepts/surface-epr.qmd) explains the quantities you will later
interpret, including why signed native port participation differs from AEDT's
nonnegative junction participation.

## Margin rows for surface EPR {#surface-epr-margin-rows}

Palace Surface EPR can report, next to each whole-surface baseline row, rows for
the part of the surface at least a given distance from the gaps. Request them
with `inset_margins_um` in the spec given to the plan's `set_surface_epr`, for
example `"inset_margins_um": (0.5, 1.0)`, and call `plan.set_surface_epr` before
`plan.prepare()`, because SGB cuts the margins into the geometry. Omit the key to
request only the baseline. Without a `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)` call, no
Surface EPR is computed. The rows are ordinary Palace attributes, so a stock Palace
executable is enough. Keys, face kinds and limits are in the
[Eigenmode contract](../reference/specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins), and the
public [Xmon EPR extension](xmon/palace.qmd) shows the source
configuration.
